rows.text: MIC's release states: '19 July 2012. The Legislative Assembly of Tonga has elected Lord Fakafanua, Noble Representative Number 1 for the Ha'apai Group, as the new Speaker of the House.' Of two nominated nobles Fakafanua received 17 votes and Lord Tu'ilakepa, Noble Representative No. 2 for Vava'u and a former Speaker, 8; the proceedings were conducted in accordance with 'Clause 15 of the Legislative Assembly Act', under which the King appoints one of the nobles as Speaker.
rows.uncertainty: The Assembly's election (its recommendation), not the royal appointment. The page was last updated on 21 November 2012, so later sentences may have been edited after 19 July; only the dated election is used.

rows.text: The same release states that 'Lord Tu'iha'ateiho was appointed as Acting Speaker during the proceedings however has now become Deputy Speaker of the House, a position which became vacant upon the appointment of Lord Tu'i'afitu as Minister of Health, earlier this month'.
rows.uncertainty: Acting service during the election proceedings: a claim only, never a Speaker holder. Who appointed him acting, and when his acting service began, are not stated. The dates of his Deputy Speakership conflict: this release and the Assembly's Tongan item of the same day (to_fakafanua_assembly_recommendation_20120719) place his recommendation as Deputy Speaker on 19 July, while an Assembly item of 2 July 2012 (a lead, listed in the report) reports him appointed Deputy Speaker that day; if the latter is right, his presiding was the Deputy Speaker presiding under the new section 16(3). The Deputy Speakership is outside this packet's role.
